item.title: Solved: How to Fix 'ImportError: cannot import name main' After Upgrading pip
item.description:
Whenever you attempt to install a package using pip, you might encounter an error similar to the following:

guru@guru-notebook:~$ pip3 install numpy
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/bin/pip3", line 9, in <module>
    from pip import main
ImportError: cannot import name 'main'

The underlying cause of this issue is often related to an upgrade in pip that results in deprecated or removed components from its internal libraries. Specifically, the shift to pip 18.0 and beyond caused several changes in its structure, leading to such import errors.

item.title: Solved: How to Fix the ImportError 'cannot import name IncompleteRead'
item.description:
When attempting to install packages using pip or pip3, you might encounter the following error message on your Ubuntu system:

$ sudo pip3 install python3-tk
Traceback (most recent call last):
 File "/usr/bin/pip3", line 9, in <module>
 load_entry_point('pip==1.5.6', 'console_scripts', 'pip3')()
 File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pkg_resources.py", line 356, in load_entry_point
 return get_distribution(dist).load_entry_point(group, name)
 File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pkg_resources.py", line 2476, in load_entry_point
 return ep.load()
 File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pip/__init__.py", line 61, in <module>
 from pip.vcs import git, mercurial, subversion, bazaar # noqa
 File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pip/vcs/mercurial.py", line 9, in <module>
 from pip.download import path_to_url
 File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/pip/download.py", line 25, in <module>
 from requests.compat import IncompleteRead
ImportError: cannot import name 'IncompleteRead'

This issue commonly arises due to a conflict between the installed versions of pip and the requests library. Specifically, the IncompleteRead class was removed from the requests package in version 2.4.0, while older versions of pip still depend on that class.
